newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria says sugar beet plantings on schedule.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria says sugar beet plantings on schedule.

text.p: Bulgaria's farmers are expected to achieve a sugar beet plantings target of 8,000 hectares this year, having sown 5,000 hectares so far, the agriculture ministry said on Tuesday.
The ministry's target is up from last year's 6,000 ha but still far below 1995's 11,200 ha. Output is forecast at 120,000 tonnes, compared with 53,000 in 1996.
"I consider the figures realistic as the planting operations are proceeding as scheduled," said Valeri Iliev, head of the plant-growing department at the ministry.
Bulgaria's sugar output fell by 64 percent in 1996 due to bad weather in the spring. Farmers had difficulties obtaining funds due to the general economic crisis in the country.

But even with the expected higher output, Bulgaria, which used to meet nearly 50 percent of its sugar needs with local production, is expected to supply its processing plants with less than 10 percent of their needs.
